LESSON: WRITING 5.3.2 WRITING LETTER SOUNDS (K-R)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.2 Writing letter sounds (k-r)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.2 Writing letter sounds (k-r), part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: What do we need to use to write letters of the alphabet? How do we write letters of the alphabet? 2. Where can we read letters of the alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.2 Writing letter sounds (k-r) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: Cooperation as learner works with others to achieve common goals in making patterns using letters of the alphabet.

● Social justice: Equity as boys and girls take equal opportunities in the group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Health education awareness as learner washes hands after modelling letters of the alphabet.

● Social cohesion under citizenship is enhanced as the learner works with others in harmony and co-operation to make patterns.

● Socio-economic awareness as learner acquire modelling skills that can be monetized.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learner relates writing in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as hearing aids and amplifiers,signed audio visual recordings, relevant

digital devices, online resources, storybooks, flashcards, charts.
